assessment: The incumbent supplies reversible, assembled organizers and checks order slips, but median time is 11 minutes and only seven of ten participants succeeded unaided. Five partition complaints suggest contents errors without establishing incidence or cause. Repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes, limiting an account that assembly is uniformly too slow; mixed-batch delays could reflect switching or complexity. Width overlap in D2-O5 limits a width-only explanation of insertion retries. No damage claims provisionally support retaining current packaging. These synthetic observations do not establish proposed mechanisms.

openings.claim: Selecting and verifying an entire order kit before insertion may reduce selection interruptions and contents errors while retaining full assembly.
openings.delta: Replace interleaved picking with reusable staging and an order-specific checklist for partition types, quantities and exterior color.
openings.prediction: Within worker and layout, staging should reduce selection/checking time or errors. Including all preparation labor may erase apparent savings.
openings.probe: Counterbalance 12 sample builds: each worker builds each layout once per workflow. Time selection, insertion, checking, packing and kit preparation separately; independently inspect contents. Use reusable spare-board aids. Confirm actual costs and available time before adoption within the fixed delivery schedule; retain ordered counts, colors, footprint, capacity and removable joints.
assumptions: Reusable aids fit the bench and budget caps.
Sample work fits available time; twelve builds provide exploratory evidence only.

openings.claim: Do short-partition difficulties persist with verified contents and a diagram explicitly depicting the ordered layout and short-partition position?
openings.delta: Distinguish location uncertainty from insertion difficulty using separate identification and insertion observations.
openings.prediction: Improved identification without improved insertion supports a guidance limitation alongside a separate insertion problem. Persistent identification errors weaken this diagram hypothesis.
openings.probe: Use ten participants and verified samples in the usual shipping state; assign five the current diagram and five an ordered-layout sketch on the existing slip, balancing layout and prior exposure. Record unaided completion, location errors and insertion retries. Include sketch labor and confirm cost caps. Subsequently verify all success targets across the 60-order pilot.
assumptions: Sketches accurately represent selected arrangements and fit existing slips without added material cost.
Ten participants cannot establish pilot success rates.
